source.title: PackProof Technical Whitepaper
source.reviewBoundary: Static, path- and date-bound source review; no repository commit identifier was present.
source.status: Technical synthesis and validation blueprint, not certification, production audit, penetration test, legal opinion, carrier attestation, or performance evidence.

classDefinitions.E: Established general proposition supported by external research or an authoritative source; not automatically PackProof performance.
classDefinitions.I: Observed in the reviewed source snapshot; still requires verification against the exact release and runtime environment.
classDefinitions.D: Proposed architecture or control not established as implemented.
classDefinitions.V: Validation target awaiting a frozen, representative, independently controlled test.
classDefinitions.P: Prohibited absolute, transferred, certified, or outcome-guarantee claim unsupported by evidence.

claims.approvedWording: Published work supports the general feasibility premise that some naturally occurring paper and print variation can support identification under the evaluated protocols.
prohibitedWording: All paper or packaging is uniquely identifiable
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: PackProof-specific replication on the target population

claims.approvedWording: Static inspection of the reviewed 0.2.1 snapshot found a substantial digital evidence design; the exact release still requires device, backend, configuration, and end-to-end verification.
prohibitedWording: The reviewed source proves production deployment
The digital evidence path is certified
The build report proves production readiness
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: exact source revision and build provenance

claims.approvedWording: The composite label-package boundary is a proposed hypothesis that may raise attack cost; it is not validated.

No production PackProof SISV comparison measurement or PackProof-specific performance result is established by the reviewed materials. Any experimental implementation is research-only until independently validated. Even after validation, PackProof may report only bounded observations under a named profile and may not infer cause, intent, actor, authenticity, custody, fraud, fault, liability, risk, or disposition.
prohibitedWording: SISV identifies who is at fault
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: implemented and frozen acquisition, eligibility, registration, feature, measurement, and neutral observation pipeline
PackProof-specific development and independently controlled blind corpora
pre-registered metrics, thresholds, subgroup, environmental, and attack analyses
all primary release criteria passed with confidence

claims.approvedWording: Physical comparison support is limited to an explicitly validated device, camera-path, OS, capture-profile, and substrate matrix.
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: camera API and OS update drift assessment

claims.approvedWording: The proposed design can return inconclusive when only partial evidence survives; its damage limits are unknown until severity-stratified validation is complete.

sourceHeadings: 9.4 Confidence bounds and the rule of three
claims.approvedWording: Report observed errors, independent-unit counts, sampling design, and confidence bounds for the exact validated scope.
Verified provider and server signals may raise assurance about app, device, account, key, and request context; they do not authenticate the package or camera scene.
prohibitedWording: Play Integrity proves a live honest capture
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: nonce, expiry, replay, account, app, and request-binding tests

claims.approvedWording: The reviewed design can prove possession of a persistent Keystore private key. Hardware-backed protection is not remotely established without full Android Key Attestation verification.
prohibitedWording: The client hardwareBacked flag is attestation

claims.approvedWording: Static inspection found an Android Keystore AES-256-GCM offline queue design; confidentiality, integrity, recoverability, and failure behavior require current real-device testing.
prohibitedWording: Offline capture is equivalent to live-attested capture
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: process death, reboot, update, reinstall, backup, key-loss, storage, and sync fault tests

claims.approvedWording: Client evidence is create-restricted and records can be tamper-evident within the stated administrative, logging, retention, and key controls; privileged paths remain.
Current HMAC-authenticated manifests are verifiable by authorized PackProof infrastructure holding the shared secret; public verification is a proposed future capability.
prohibitedWording: Anyone can independently verify the HMAC
Current dossiers use a public digital signature
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: published key, certificate, and status metadata
public verifier and cross-language test vectors
rotation, revocation, and long-term verification policy

claims.approvedWording: Challenge-directed capture, timing, telemetry, and attestation are bounded signals intended to raise replay cost; attack performance is unvalidated.
Support is limited to explicitly validated device, camera-path, capture-profile, and substrate classes.
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: documented revalidation after relevant platform changes

claims.approvedWording: The architecture is mapped to identified standards and guidance as readiness targets; conformity, certification, accreditation, and endorsement have not been established.
prohibitedWording: FIPS compliant because an algorithm is used
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: current normative text and defined scope
exact validated cryptographic module and operating boundary where required

claims.approvedWording: A properly founded PackProof dossier may support authentication; admissibility, legal effect, and evidentiary weight are case-, jurisdiction-, purpose-, and procedure-specific.
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: decision by the relevant court or tribunal

claims.approvedWording: PackProof may help organize reason-code-specific evidence for submission; the issuer, network, marketplace, or platform remains the decision-maker.
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: representative independently auditable historical outcome study
stratification by reason code, network, issuer, region, merchant type, selection, and policy version
continued disclaimer that future outcomes are not guaranteed

claims.approvedWording: A visible boundary-mark and evidence-notice protocol is designed to make a transaction record more deliberate, visible, and reviewable, and may discourage opportunistic misrepresentation. PackProof has not established a deterrence or fraud-reduction rate.
prohibitedWording: Makes the seller a fraud-proof target
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: reported counts, uncertainty, population, exclusions, time window, and limitations

claims.approvedWording: PackProof can preserve seller reference and buyer arrival views of the marked label-package boundary, tape, seams, and surrounding package for side-by-side human review. A reviewer may describe visible continuity, variance, or an inability to assess; PackProof does not infer cause, intent, actor, authenticity, custody, fraud, fault, or disposition.
prohibitedWording: A broken seam proves the package was opened
A visible difference catches the seller
Matching tape proves the same package
The seam identifies who is at fault
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: exact two-device workflow verified on the release candidate
neutral reviewer vocabulary and limitations displayed
accessibility, capture-completion, and dossier usability tests

claims.approvedWording: The launch product records user-supplied carrier and tracking fields and may preserve label observations. Contracted carrier weight, dimension, intake, possession, route, and delivery telemetry are future integrations and, if implemented, would remain sourced neutral context rather than a finding about conduct.
prohibitedWording: PackProof proves the parcel weight at handoff
A weight difference identifies who swapped the contents
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: contracted provider integration and source provenance
defined measurement, correction, time, unit, and uncertainty semantics
neutral presentation that does not infer actor, cause, fraud, or fault

claims.approvedWording: Production evidence is collected to provide the operational service described to participants; it is not automatically a model-training dataset. SISV research requires a separate affirmative opt-in, a defined research purpose, minimization and redaction, operational/research separation, retention and deletion controls, withdrawal behavior, lineage, and audited access.
prohibitedWording: Users passively build PackProof's proprietary dataset
PackProof can reuse evidence for any research purpose
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: privacy, data-protection, biometric and jurisdictional review as applicable
purpose limitation, minimization, redaction, retention, deletion, withdrawal, and legal-hold policy
separate research storage, lineage, labeling, versioning, and access audit

claims.approvedWording: A smartphone-first workflow may avoid dedicated authentication hardware for supported users; software, cloud, operations, devices, training, integrations, validation, audit, legal, and incident-response costs remain.
prohibitedWording: No hardware required for every deployment

claims.approvedWording: PackProof records and preserves the evidence and sourced events it actually observes. Corroborating identifiers, procedures, carrier data, and human review are required for broader conclusions.
prohibitedWording: Proves complete physical chain of custody
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: separately defined corroborating system and claim
independent validation appropriate to that new claim

claims.approvedWording: Offline evidence carries device wall-clock and relative-time observations plus later server receipt/finalization provenance; it does not generally establish a trusted absolute capture time.
prohibitedWording: Later synchronization proves the original capture time
requiredEvidenceToAdvance: separately specified trusted hardware or external time service
independent verification of its threat model and operating limits
